test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 01 Jul, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Writ of Mandamus is a Fundamental Right classifiable under:

options.text: the right to freedom of religion

solution:
The correct answer is __**constitutional remedies**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Writ of Mandamus** is a judicial remedy in the form of an order from a court to any government, subordinate court, corporation, or public authority to do some specific act which that body is obliged under law to do.
 
• It is classified under **constitutional remedies**, which is a fundamental right provided under **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 32 provides the right to individuals to move to the Supreme Court for enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• The **Writ of Mandamus** can be issued to enforce the performance of public duties by public authorities and to ensure that they fulfill their legal obligations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** provides for five types of writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto, and Certiorari.
 
• These writs are a crucial part of the **judicial review mechanism** in India, ensuring the protection of citizens' rights against any arbitrary actions of the state.
 
• The **right to constitutional remedies** is considered the heart and soul of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, as it is the protector and guarantor of all other fundamental rights.
 
• Article 32 is also known as the "Right to Constitutional Remedies" and is a fundamental right that cannot be suspended, except in cases of emergency as declared by the President of India.
